summary_paragraph: John, a man with a history of hypertension and alcohol use disorder, was admitted after a heavy drinking episode involving a gallon of vodka, presenting with atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. He reported forgetting and not picking up his medications after a recent discharge. On admission, his heart rate was elevated at 130s, and he was treated with IV and oral diltiazem, followed by the addition of metoprolol to achieve rate control under 100. His chest pain was attributed to chest wall tenderness and gastritis, with normal cardiac enzymes and a clear chest X-ray. He received diazepam per CIWA protocol for alcohol withdrawal prevention, along with thiamine, folic acid, and multivitamins. Abdominal pain resolved with supportive care. By discharge, he was stable, alert, and ambulatory, with a simplified medication regimen including Campral to support alcohol cessation. He planned to engage in outpatient treatment and was discharged home with follow-up instructions.
problems: Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
